title: chore(objectui): bump the console pin past objectui f624f278 (objectui#11553), carrying objectui#11544 and objectui#11562 too — #12438 B1 and #21464's `columns` hold wait on it
body:
Filed by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015, `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`), as the install-face carrier the unlock scan needs. This repo consumes objectui through `.objectui-sha`, so a card waiting on an objectui landing unlocks on the pin, not on the objectui merge (the rule applied on #20313 and #20936). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Graded here: `tooling` · `priority:p2` · `domain:devx` · `pm:queue`. It has the grade of the last bump card, #20949.

## Measured now

- `.objectui-sha` on `origin/main` `83b3d32020` is `89cad75d5570`, set by PR #21380's bump on 2026-10-02.
- objectui `main` is 63 commits ahead of it. `compare f624f278...89cad75d5570` answers `behind_by: 63`.
- No open card or PR in this repo moves the pin: all open issues and PRs were listed and their titles grepped for `objectui-sha` and pin bump, with 0 hits.

## What waits on the pin

| objectui landing | merged | who waits here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| objectui#11553 (Studio surfaces package-less flows), PR objectui#11565 → `f624f278` | 2026-10-03 | **#12438** B1's re-run (`Blocked-by:` is re-derived to this card) |
| objectui#11544 (the grid's group headers stop reading `columns[].options`) | 2026-10-03 | **#21464**'s held object-grid `columns` member, typed by reference once the pin carries it |
| objectui#11562 (inline `textarea` keeps its line breaks) | 2026-10-03 | the console this repo ships; no card is gated on it |

#21596's run is taken on a console built at the current pin, so it reads whatever this bump carries.

## Scope

- Bump to objectui `main` at claim time, at or past `f624f278`. Re-measure each citation the bump moves, as the previous bump PRs did.
- The PR body names each carried landing above, with its merge commit.
- ⛔ No objectui edit. ⛔ No ride-along code change beyond what the bump's own gates require.

## Done when

The pin carries `f624f278`. The unlock scan then returns #12438 to its seat, and #21464's seat reads the `columns` hold against the new pin.
